problem: The unit check is wrong. It says "m^{1.25} in the denominator cancels against √P and leaves a plain number", but P is a power in kW, so √P has units kW^0.5, not metres. Nothing cancels, and N√P/H^{5/4} is not dimensionless (its units are rpm·kW^0.5·m^-1.25). A student who follows this check will believe specific speed is dimensionless, which contradicts the later statement that the dimensionless form is ω√Q/(gH)^{3/4}.
fix: Drop the unit-cancelling claim. Say instead: the 5/4 exponent cannot be found by cancelling units, because N_s in this metric form is not dimensionless; get it by combining N ∝ √H/D with P ∝ D²H^{3/2}, or simply remember it. Only ω√Q/(gH)^{3/4} is dimensionless.

where: Section 2, note under the N_s formula
problem: Calling N_s "a plain number" sits badly next to "quoted in rpm" and with the later sentence that only ω√Q/(gH)^{3/4} has the units divided out. Readers may conclude the rpm form is dimensionless.
fix: Say: in this metric form it carries units of rpm, but it is not a running speed; only the form ω√Q/(gH)^{3/4} is fully dimensionless.

problem: The wording is muddled. It sets up "not √(N P)" but then finishes with "not 5000", mixing two different mistakes: forgetting the square root on P (70.71 instead of 5000) and taking the root of the whole product (√(300 × 5000) = 1224.7).
fix: State one mistake at a time: "N√P means N times √P. With P = 5000 kW, √P = 70.71, so the numerator is 300 × 70.71 = 21213. Writing √(N P) would wrongly give √1500000 = 1224.7."

problem: The worked example is summarised as giving "unit quantities of 33.54 rpm and 0.805 m³/s", but three unit quantities were computed; unit power 6.988 kW is dropped.
fix: Write: unit speed 33.54 rpm, unit discharge 0.805 m³/s and unit power 6.988 kW.
